title: Unauthenticated Account Takeover via User Switch Endpoint
description: The POST /api/users/switch endpoint permitted any unauthenticated client to specify an arbitrary targetUserId and receive a valid 7-day signed JWT authentication cookie, completely bypassing password authentication and compromising any user account.
root_cause: Desktop Electron developer convenience feature left unauthenticated on the public Express server without credential verification.
intended_behavior: User switching must strictly require valid credential authentication, or the endpoint must be completely removed in production web environments.

trace.description: Incoming unauthenticated POST request with targetUserId in body
Locates arbitrary target user in database without verifying caller credentials
Signs and issues JWT session cookie giving full access to victim account

evidence.description: jwt.sign called with targetUser claims without verifying password or session origin

conditions.description: Attacker is completely unauthenticated and only requires knowledge of a user ID

execution.attacker_perspective: External unauthenticated attacker targeting arbitrary user accounts
instructions: Send HTTP POST /api/users/switch with JSON payload containing targetUserId
Inspect Set-Cookie header in response containing authenticated session token for victim
execution.observed_result: Server returned 200 OK and valid JWT cookie impersonating victim

remediation.strategy: Eliminate the unauthenticated /api/users/switch endpoint and require standard credential-based authentication for all login sessions.

code_changes.fixed_code: Endpoint removed entirely. User switching redirects to standard /login with credentials.

likelihood.reason: Trivially exploitable over network with zero authentication or brute force required

impact.reason: Complete account takeover and unauthorized access to all user code workspaces and data

confidence.reason: Directly confirmed from source inspection and execution flow

title: Sensitive Information Disclosure and User Account Enumeration
description: The GET /api/users/profiles route and the login page rendered list of all registered users including userIds and email addresses without authentication.
root_cause: Desktop profile quick-switcher queried all database users and passed their credentials and IDs to unauthenticated clients.
intended_behavior: User identifiers and email addresses must not be exposed to unauthenticated users or public endpoints.

trace.description: Unauthenticated client requests list of all user profiles
Queries all users in database and serializes identifiers and emails
Returns full user list to unauthenticated requester

evidence.description: Unrestricted User.find query returns all user records to public caller

execution.attacker_perspective: Unauthenticated reconnaissance agent scraping user directories
instructions: Read JSON array containing all registered usernames, emails, and persistent userIds
execution.observed_result: Received complete roster of registered user accounts and identifiers

remediation.strategy: Remove the public profile enumeration route and remove user enumeration from the login page view.

code_changes.fixed_code: Route removed. Login page renders standard authentication form without user listing.

likelihood.reason: Accessible via simple GET request with no parameters or headers needed

impact.reason: Exposes PII and user enumeration data facilitating spear phishing and account targeting

confidence.reason: Confirmed via source code review and API definition

title: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution Proxy and Resource Exhaustion
description: The POST /runCode endpoint was completely unauthenticated, allowing anonymous internet users to submit arbitrary source code for execution via the server's backend Judge0 integration.
root_cause: Missing authentication middleware on POST /runCode endpoint.
intended_behavior: Only authenticated users with a valid JWT session should be permitted to execute code.

trace.description: Anonymous client posts code payload to execution endpoint
Passes arbitrary code directly to execution backend without verifying session
Submits code to Judge0 using server RapidAPI credentials

execution.attacker_perspective: Unauthenticated third party abusing code runner as free compute or bot proxy
instructions: Send HTTP POST /runCode with code payload and no authentication headers or cookies
execution.observed_result: Server processed request and returned execution output using server API quota

likelihood.reason: Exposed endpoint with straightforward JSON contract

impact.reason: Exhausts paid RapidAPI quota, risks API key revocation, and exposes compute backend to abuse

title: Unauthenticated AI Assistant Resource Exhaustion via HTTP and WebSocket
description: The POST /ask-ai endpoint and the Socket.IO connection handler accepted connections and AI inference requests without verifying user authentication, allowing anyone to exhaust LLM resources.
root_cause: Missing authentication checks on /ask-ai route and missing io.use authentication middleware on Socket.IO server.
intended_behavior: All AI inference interfaces must require valid user authentication before processing queries.

trace.description: Anonymous socket connection established without handshake authentication
Socket listener triggers runTeacherAgent without verifying caller identity
Dispatches queries to local/cloud Ollama using server GPU and API keys

evidence.description: Socket.IO connection handler lacked io.use authentication middleware

execution.attacker_perspective: Unauthenticated attacker flooding AI agent requests
instructions: Emit ask-ai event with arbitrary prompt payload
execution.observed_result: Server invoked LangChain agent and streamed responses to unauthenticated socket

remediation.strategy: Enforce authenticate middleware on /ask-ai HTTP endpoint and io.use JWT cookie verification on Socket.IO.

likelihood.reason: Directly accessible via HTTP and WebSocket without credentials

impact.reason: Exhausts Ollama cloud API quotas and overloads server CPU/GPU resources

confidence.reason: Confirmed across HTTP and WebSocket paths

title: Cross-Site Scripting via Unsandboxed Same-Origin HTML Preview
description: The GET /preview/:id endpoint served user-generated HTML, CSS, and JavaScript directly under the application origin with a permissive CSP that permitted unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval without sandbox isolation.
root_cause: HTML preview was rendered on same origin without CSP sandbox directive.
intended_behavior: User-generated preview pages must be sandboxed into an opaque origin using CSP sandbox to isolate them from application cookies, storage, and APIs.

trace.description: User submits arbitrary HTML, CSS, and JS code
Stores user HTML document for preview access
Delivers untrusted HTML under main origin without sandbox isolation

evidence.description: CSP header omitted 'sandbox allow-scripts allow-forms' directive

conditions.description: User opens HTML preview containing crafted script payload

execution.attacker_perspective: Attacker sharing a malicious project or workspace containing preview payload
instructions: Open project containing script accessing localStorage or authenticated origin APIs
execution.observed_result: Preview script executed in same origin context and could access same-origin endpoints

remediation.strategy: Add 'sandbox allow-scripts allow-forms' to Content-Security-Policy on /preview/:id to isolate preview in opaque origin.

code_changes.fixed_code: res.setHeader('Content-Security-Policy', 'sandbox allow-scripts allow-forms; default-src \'none\'; script-src \'unsafe-inline\'; style-src \'unsafe-inline\'; img-src data: https: blob:; font-src data: https:;');

likelihood.reason: Requires user to trigger preview or preview malicious shared workspace

impact.reason: Potential theft of localStorage data or actions performed on behalf of authenticated user

confidence.reason: Confirmed by preview route response header analysis

title: Sibling Directory Traversal in File Upload Deletion Utility
description: In safeDeleteUpload, targetFilePath.startsWith(allowedDir) was evaluated where allowedDir did not terminate with a path separator, allowing potential matching of sibling directories sharing the same prefix.
root_cause: Path prefix comparison omitted trailing path.sep delimiter.
intended_behavior: Path containment checks must enforce that targetFilePath is strictly inside allowedDir with proper boundary separator.

trace.description: File deletion helper called with fileUrl parameter
Resolves target path against public uploads directory
Evaluates prefix containment without trailing separator

conditions.description: Manipulated database fileUrl pointing to sibling path

execution.attacker_perspective: Attacker manipulating fileUrl in document record
instructions: Provide file URL targeting sibling directory with matching prefix
execution.observed_result: Prefix check validated true because allowedDir prefix matched sibling directory name

remediation.strategy: Append path.sep to allowedDir in safeDeleteUpload to ensure strict folder boundary containment.

likelihood.reason: Requires manipulating fileUrl attribute in database record

impact.reason: Unintended deletion of files in sibling directories

confidence.reason: Confirmed by static analysis of path comparison

title: DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via File Name Tab Rendering
description: In editor.js, active tab markup was constructed by string-concatenating file.name directly into an innerHTML template without HTML entity escaping.
root_cause: Direct interpolation of file.name into tabContainer.innerHTML string template.
intended_behavior: All dynamic strings rendered into HTML templates must be properly entity-escaped or inserted using textContent.

trace.description: Iterates open tab IDs and retrieves file item
Directly interpolates unescaped file.name into attribute and span
Assigns unescaped markup to DOM innerHTML

evidence.description: file.name interpolated directly into HTML template assigned to innerHTML

conditions.description: User opens an imported folder or zip archive containing crafted file names with HTML special characters

execution.attacker_perspective: Attacker providing a zip archive with crafted filename payload
instructions: Create file named '.js' in workspace
Open file into an editor tab
execution.observed_result: Raw HTML tags rendered into tab bar instead of plain text

remediation.strategy: Apply escapeHtml helper to file.name and file.id before rendering into tab HTML template.

code_changes.fixed_code: const safeName = escapeHtml(file.name); const safeId = escapeHtml(file.id); ...

likelihood.reason: Requires user to import a folder or zip containing maliciously named files

impact.reason: Execution of script in user context upon opening malicious file tab
